findings.quote: `_urllib3_request_context()` in `src/requests/adapters.py` (the new `elif verify is True:` branch, about line 94) puts the module-level `_preloaded_ssl_context` (defined at lines 75-78) into `pool_kwargs["ssl_context"]` for every `verify=True` request. urllib3's `ssl_wrap_socket()` (`urllib3/util/ssl_.py`, around lines 407-433) and `_ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname()` (`urllib3/connection.py`, around lines 1040-1056) treat a supplied context as the object to configure: they call `context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile)` when the pool has a `cert_file`, set `context.verify_mode`, set `context.check_hostname = False` when `assert_hostname` or `assert_fingerprint` is in play, and call `set_alpn_protocols`. Before this PR each pool got its own fresh context, so none of that could cross requests. Now a call such as `requests.get(url_a, cert=("a.crt", "a.key"))` loads client identity A into the one context that every later `verify=True` request in the process uses, for any host, and two threads using different client certs race on the same context so the wrong certificate can be presented. The pool key separates pools by `cert_file`, but the context is shared by all of them, so the isolation that the pool key was supposed to provide is silently defeated. The same applies to an `HTTPAdapter` subclass that passes `assert_hostname=False` through `init_poolmanager`, which would turn off hostname checking on the shared context for every other verify=True consumer. The remedy is to keep the "load once" win without sharing the mutable object: load the bundle once into a template and give each pool its own context, or only supply the shared context when no client cert and no other TLS option is in `pool_kwargs`, and fall back to the old per-pool path otherwise. A cleaner variant is to cache a context per distinct TLS-settings tuple (bundle, client cert) so that a context is shared only between requests that would have configured it identically.
findings.title: A single shared `SSLContext` is mutated by urllib3 on every connection, including client certificates (highest severity)

findings.quote: Lines 75-78 of `src/requests/adapters.py` now run `create_urllib3_context()`, `extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` and `load_verify_locations()` when `requests.adapters` is imported. Every user pays the bundle-load cost at `import requests`, including users who only ever call with `verify=False`, and the extraction of a zipped certifi to a temp directory now happens at import rather than at first use. The old `cert_verify()` raised a deliberate `OSError("Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle, invalid path: ...")` when the default bundle was missing; with this change that guard is gone for `verify=True`, and the same situation becomes an uncatchable-at-import `FileNotFoundError` or `ssl.SSLError` that breaks `import requests` entirely (for example in stripped-down or vendored deployments where certifi's file is removed but the user passes their own bundle). The remedy is a lazily initialised, cached accessor (a small function using `functools.lru_cache` or a first-use module global with a lock) so that the cost is paid on first `verify=True` use, errors surface at request time with the original message, and importing the package stays free of side effects.
findings.title: Import-time work and a lost error path for a missing default bundle

findings.quote: `_urllib3_request_context()` now decides between `ca_certs` and `ca_cert_dir` with `os.path.isdir(verify)`, and `cert_verify()` (lines 297-317) still decides the same thing again with `os.path.exists` and `os.path.isdir` and sets the same two attributes on the connection. The PR description itself says the `conn.ca_certs` assignment may no longer be needed. Both functions are called back to back from `send()` (`_get_connection()` then `cert_verify()`), so for a string `verify` the pool is configured by one and the connection re-configured by the other. `cert_verify()` also gained a nested `if verify is not True:` with a comment saying "verify must be a str then", plus the `cert_reqs` assignment moved ahead of it, which makes a previously linear function harder to scan. The code-judo move is to give the path-to-kwargs mapping a single home, for example a helper `_ca_kwargs(verify)` returning `{"ssl_context": ...}`, `{"ca_certs": ...}`, `{"ca_cert_dir": ...}` or `{}` and used by `_urllib3_request_context()` only. `cert_verify()` should then keep only what its public subclass-facing contract requires: the existence check that raises `OSError`, the `cert_reqs` assignment, and the client-cert handling. Because `cert_verify()` is a documented extension point that third-party adapters override, keep the method, but delete the duplicated attribute-setting inside it.
findings.title: The `verify` path classification is now implemented twice, and the old copy is half-dead (missed code-judo)

findings.quote: The diff touches only `src/requests/adapters.py`. Nothing asserts that `verify=True` reuses one context, that a directory `verify` produces `ca_cert_dir`, that a missing bundle path still raises `OSError`, or that a client certificate does not leak between requests (finding 1). The author noted they could not see how to inspect the context from a request; a unit test of `_urllib3_request_context()` return values and of `poolmanager.connection_from_host(...)` pool identity is possible without the network and would also have exposed finding 1. Add those tests together with the fix for finding 1.
findings.title: No test covers the new behaviour
